inputs.prompt:
<Picture 1> is the authoritative spatial map of the world, not a visual-style reference. Treat it as a top-down geometric specification that must be converted into a street-level 3D world. Do not imitate the visual appearance of the map. Infer plausible 3D buildings, roads and vegetation while preserving the 2D spatial relationships: road topology, intersections, building blocks, open areas and vegetation zones.

The camera follows this EXACT timeline (total 5.2 seconds, 24 fps):
- 0.0s-2.0s: ride straight forward along the street at cycling speed, buildings on both sides.
- 2.0s-4.0s: reach the intersection and turn LEFT by 90 degrees at a constant smooth rate. The whole view rotates left: the street ahead sweeps toward the right edge of the frame while the crossing street enters from the left and becomes the new heading.
- 4.0s-5.2s: ride straight forward along the new street, buildings on both sides.

The left turn is MANDATORY. The heading at 5.2s must point 90 degrees to the LEFT of the heading at 0.0s. Do not keep going straight through the intersection.

Generation task: a continuous, photorealistic first-person bicycle journey through the world specified by <Picture 1>. Camera height about 1.6 meters, smooth forward motion, natural head stabilization, realistic parallax, no cuts, no drone shots, no viewpoint changes.

Visual quality: realistic urban environment, physically plausible scale, realistic architecture, materials and daylight, detailed road surface, sidewalks, trees and facades, coherent perspective.

Hard constraints: the map controls the world layout; the timeline above controls camera motion. Do not show the map itself inside the generated environment. Prioritize executing the left turn over cinematic composition.
